view: This print trades on the outlook: the FY revenue guide and what management says about Q4 and 2027 China funding and credit. The industry state that outlook has to describe was disclosed by the largest peer a day ago and it got worse. On its 11-24 call QFIN said its Q3 volume fell 22% QoQ and 41% YoY. It guided Q4 volume down about 20% QoQ and Q4 non-GAAP profit 16-40% below Q3. It said industry liquidity will tighten further for one or two quarters, D1 delinquency and C-M2 have not turned, more rules on entry, partnerships and funding are pending, on-balance-sheet pricing goes to 4x LPR by end-2027, and 2027 volume cannot be forecast. FINV's own Q2 call (2026-08-27) had already shown it is hit harder in China than QFIN in the quarter: China origination was down about 50% in July, funding costs were rising, and the collection campaign was hurting recoveries. Only the overseas leg (27% of revenue, growing) offsets this. In each of the last four cycles FINV's print reaction carried the same sign as QFIN's. The August analog is the same setup as today: a sympathy drop of about 4.5% on QFIN's day, then a further drop of about 15% on its own print. Against that, the bar is now lower than in August. The sell-side has cut FY EPS 36% in a month and put revenue below the guide's low end. QFIN's disclosed elasticity (revenue -13% QoQ on volume -22%, because revenue follows the balance more than new volume) suggests FINV could still reach about RMB11.5bn and reaffirm the low end. Shrinking volume also lowers upfront provisioning, which can flatter Q3 profit. And a larger buyback is possible at a market cap well below the cash and liquid assets management cited (RMB7.5bn plus about RMB5bn). Netting it, the deciding line, the Q4 and 2027 tone, leans negative beyond what today's sympathy move took. I lean down but not far enough to recommend.
unpriced: Possibly the second leg of the read-through. FINV took only about 45% of QFIN's move today, but its China volume fell harder than QFIN's in Q3, and its call will have to repeat QFIN's outlook: tighter liquidity, rising credit and collection costs, pending rules, no 2027 visibility. In August the same sympathy-then-own-print pattern left a further -15%. The bias is the market treating the peer read-through as fully absorbed on the peer's day. Partly offset by fresh consensus cuts that already sit below the guide's low end.

recommendation.reason: QFIN's 11-24 call disclosed a worsening industry state into Q4: tighter liquidity ahead, Q4 volume down about 20% QoQ, credit not yet turned, and more rules pending. FINV's call must describe the same state with a China book that shrank faster. Its reactions have matched QFIN's sign over four cycles, and in August the sympathy day left a further -15%. But the sell-side cut FINV's FY EPS 36% in a month and already models revenue below the guide's low end, and today's -4.4% on heavy volume took part of the read-through. So the edge is a lean, not a 65% call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The FY revenue guide reaffirmed at RMB11.5bn or more (above the 11.31bn consensus), with Q3 profit well above the roughly RMB200m-a-quarter that consensus implies for H2, and/or a new or enlarged buyback sized against the sub-cash market cap.

self_critique: The bar has fallen a long way. The sell-side cut EPS 36% in a month and models revenue below the guide's low end, the stock is down about 52% since August and trades below the liquid assets management cited, and today's heavy-volume sympathy drop may have cleared the sellers. QFIN's elasticity says FINV's revenue can hold up better than its volume, and contraction accounting can produce a Q3 profit beat. A reaffirmed RMB11.5bn guide plus a bigger buyback could squeeze a thin, washed-out ADS on a half-day Friday open. The four-cycle co-movement with QFIN is only four observations and partly reflects the same news being priced twice. Weighed: the down side rests on dated disclosures about Q4 that FINV's call cannot avoid repeating, while the up side rests on inference about FINV's revenue mix and a possible buyback. So I keep the lean but hold it short of a recommendation.
